claims.text: A conformal ultrathin Pt shell on Ni or Cu nanoparticle cores supported on CeO2 will improve catalytic activity relative to conventional dispersed Pt catalysts.
The proposed core-shell catalyst will improve durability under automotive exhaust conditions relative to conventional dispersed Pt catalysts.
The proposed architecture will reduce platinum-group-metal consumption relative to conventional dispersed Pt catalysts.
Atomic layer deposition or controlled chemical reduction can produce a conformal and robust 1–2-atomic-layer Pt shell on preformed Ni or Cu nanoparticles.
The Pt shell will be electronically coupled to the Ni or Cu core.
Strong metal-support interactions with CeO2 will stabilize the core-shell nanoparticles.
The underlying Ni or Cu core will modify the electronic structure of the ultrathin Pt overlayer.
The Pt/Ni-or-Cu/CeO2 architecture will enhance oxygen storage.
The Pt/Ni-or-Cu/CeO2 architecture will resist sintering during high-temperature operation.
The ultrathin Pt layer will provide active sites for CO oxidation, hydrocarbon oxidation, and NOx reduction.
Electronic tuning of Pt by the Ni or Cu core will optimize reactant adsorption.
CeO2 will provide oxygen buffering that stabilizes the active sites.
Electronic tuning, oxygen buffering, and stabilization against sintering will collectively increase catalytic efficiency at lower Pt loading.
The same mechanisms will extend catalyst lifetime during thermal and redox aging.
The core-shell catalyst will retain greater activity and structural integrity after accelerated thermal and redox aging than dispersed Pt on an oxide support.
Performance benefits may diminish outside the tested temperature or reactant-composition ranges.
Performance benefits depend on maintaining a uniform and stable Pt shell during prolonged high-temperature redox cycling.
